letter.md · from Varnika
Dear Varun,

Happy 31st. I have started this letter more times than I want to admit, which is funny, because talking to you has never been hard. I think it's because there's so much I want to get right.

When I moved to Bangalore for Christ, I knew I would miss home. I didn't expect how much I would miss you specifically. The late night conversations. The random dog videos. The way you'd explain something complicated until it suddenly made sense. Somewhere between new classes and a new city, we got a little quieter with each other. Nothing broke. Distance just has a way of turning "every day" into "we should catch up soon."

So think of this as my patch. A small fix for something that matters a lot.

I am so proud of you. Proud of the engineer you've become, quietly solving problems most people can't even describe. And prouder still of the man you are at 31: kind without making a show of it, curious about everything from clean code to a bird call nobody else noticed, and steady in a way that makes the people around you feel safe. I look up to you more than I have ever said out loud.

Going through our photos for this, I noticed the same thing in almost all of them. A tiny me holding a rabbit nearly as big as I was, with you right beside me. The two of us on a watchtower at sunrise, cameras ready. You sitting patiently through my aarti on Rakhi. Different years, different places, same big brother, always right there.

No matter how busy life gets, with your deadlines, my exams, and whatever comes next for both of us, we are a team. That was true when we were kids. It's true now, with a map between us. And it will be true on every trail we haven't hiked yet.

You are loved. You are valued. And you are, without question, the best brother I could have asked for.

Always your sister, and your biggest fan,
Varnika
P.S.Give Don and Diana a belly rub from me. They're allowed to miss you, just not more than I do.
